states.edition: No statewide residential (IRC) code for owner-occupied one- and two-family dwellings. The 2025 Vermont Fire & Building Safety Code (effective Nov 4, 2025; NFPA 1 and NFPA 101 2021, IBC/IEBC 2021) covers 'public buildings', which include rented one- and two-family homes and ADUs. RBES energy code applies statewide.
states.differs_from_app: 'Burlington adopts the IRC' is wrong. Burlington Code of Ordinances §8-2 adopts the Vermont Fire & Building Safety Code (2025 VFBSC: NFPA 1/101 2021 + IBC/IEBC 2021) for all buildings, and its department lists no IRC; Rutland City (§1024) does the same. The 'local' kind and 'no residential code beyond fire and energy' are right only for owner-occupied single-family homes. Rented one- and two-family homes are regulated by the Division of Fire Safety (construction permit required). Where the VFBSC applies, its values differ from the IRC: guards 42 in. (NFPA 101), stairs 7-3/4 in. / 10 in. allowed for one- and two-family dwellings, frost depth at least 5 ft, and a statewide ground-snow-load map by town (40-70 psf).
notes: Owner-occupied single-family projects need no state construction permit (VFBSC permit matrix), though a city like Burlington or Rutland may still require a local building permit.
For one- and two-family dwellings under the VFBSC, Vermont amendment 101:24.2.5.7 permits 7-3/4 in. max risers and 10 in. min treads in new construction.

Guards under the VFBSC follow NFPA 101: at least 42 in. high, with no opening that passes a 4 in. sphere up to 34 in. (DFS code sheet). The 2025 code's window-balcony rule also calls 42 in. the standard guard height.
VFBSC amends IBC 1809.5: foundations must reach below the local frost line but not less than 5 ft below finished grade.

VFBSC Annex V sets minimum ground snow loads by town (40/50/60/70 psf). Above 2,500 ft elevation the authority having jurisdiction sets the value. The minimum roof snow load is 40 psf on roofs of 5 degrees or less, and Cs times 40 psf on steeper roofs.
H.718 (2026) passed the House on Apr 24, 2026 and would have the Director of Fire Safety assess adopting a residential code by Jan 15, 2027. Its final status was not confirmed.

counties.jurisdiction: City of Philadelphia Department of Licenses and Inspections (L&I)
counties.edition: 2021 IRC as amended by the PA UCC and the Philadelphia Code, Title 4 (Philadelphia Residential Code); the 2021 codes took effect Jan 1, 2026 and are required for every application filed on or after July 1, 2026
counties.wind_basis: L&I states only that Philadelphia design wind speeds are above 110 mph (2021 IRC ultimate design wind speed); no exact value is published
deck_notes: Decks less than 12 in above grade, and not over a basement or other story, need no permit; higher decks need zoning and building permits.
A site plan is required if the deck is over 216 sq ft, above the first floor, or in a front or side yard.
Construction plans are required if the deck is over 216 sq ft or above the first floor.
EZ deck permit (no plans) covers only rear-yard, first-floor decks attached to an existing single-family house.
EZ decks are limited to 160 sq ft, or 216 sq ft with intermediate posts, with no roof and no hot tub.
EZ decks need 3 ft clearance to the rear lot line and posts at least 1'-6" from all lot lines.
Footings go 30 in below grade on undisturbed soil, at least 6 in thick, 16 in diameter at end posts and 19 in at intermediate posts.
EZ framing: posts at least 6x6 with 2x4 diagonal bracing, pressure-treated Southern Pine, and hot-dipped galvanized or stainless hardware.
The ledger is fastened with 1/2 in fasteners at 16 in on center, staggered, and may not bear on stone or masonry veneer.
Guards are required over 30 in above grade: 36 to 42 in high with no opening over 4 in, and 4x4 guard posts may not be notched.
EZ stairs need risers of at most 7 3/4 in, treads of at least 10 in and handrails 34 to 38 in, stricter than the PA UCC's 8 1/4 / 9.
Under the EZ permit, stairs to grade are allowed only on detached or semi-detached houses.
counties.note: The 30 in frost line comes from L&I's EZ Deck Permit standard (rev. 8/26, IRC-2021). L&I documents give no ground snow, wind speed or seismic category. Its 2021 IRC FAQ says live load, not snow, governs deck design in Philadelphia, and its webinar slides say only that wind speeds exceed 110 mph.
